summary: End-to-end verification of the three follow-ups on Bright Blessing: SPAM protection (quote/app/nomination screens, timing trap, honeypot, rate limit, delivery-health exclusion, 'Not spam' restore + email), CSV EXPORT (/api/admin/nominations/export headers, auth, spam-exclusion, cycle filter, UI download), and ANNOUNCEMENTS (server-side first-name trim, 400 on missing fields, publish round-trip, public blessings-honored, admin panel add/toggle/delete). BACKEND: added /app/backend/tests/test_spam_export_announcements.py (16 tests) — ALL 16 PASS in isolation (24s). Verifies: spam content on all three forms is stored with spam=true + spam_reason and NEVER emailed (no delivery.email.status; 'filtered as spam' logged, no 'Support notification sent' for that id); timing trap (elapsed_ms=300) returns {success:true} with no id and stores nothing; honeypot (company set) same; rate limit allows at most 4/IP in window; genuine lead (elapsed_ms 45000) stored with spam not set and delivery.email.status='sent'; POST /api/admin/quotes/{id}/not-spam requires auth, flips spam→false and triggers email (delivery.email.status='sent'); /api/admin/delivery-health undelivered count ignores spam items; /api/admin/nominations/export: 401/403 without token, text/csv + Content-Disposition attachment + exact 11-column header, excludes spam rows, includes non-spam, ?cycle=1999-01 filter narrows to header only; /api/admin/announcements: first_name 'Dana Hughes' server-trimmed to 'Dana', missing first/city → 400, created published=False and absent from public GET /api/announcements, PATCH ?published=true makes it appear publicly then false hides it, admin GET/DELETE require auth. FRONTEND (preview URL, brightadmin/Dallas2025!!): /admin → spam-group details element renders with summary 'Filtered as spam (1) — not emailed to you'; opening reveals not-spam-{id} and delete-submission-{id} buttons; spam item does NOT appear in main submission list. Clicking not-spam moves item to main list AND backend reports delivery.email.status='sent' + spam=false. Nominations tab shows export-nominators button → click triggers CSV download (filename bright-blessing-nominators.csv). Announcements-panel accepts first_name='Dana Hughes', city='Plano', note; after save: server stored first_name='Dana' (confirmed via API), published=false, toggle label 'Draft', delete button present. Clicking toggle publishes server-side (verified via public /bright-blessing showing blessings-honored with 'Dana' + 'Plano' and NO 'Hughes'). Delete via UI removes it. Regression: /bright-blessing nomination form still renders (bb-nominator-name, bb-submit); delivery-health-banner still renders on admin; publish toggle left OFF at end; zero console errors. Noted minor UI issue: announcement toggle button inner text ('Draft'/'Showing') is briefly stale right after click (data in DB is correct, loadAnnouncements re-fetch latency); recovers on next mount. No critical bugs.

minor.issue: Because every /api/* request from the preview environment arrives from the k8s ingress with the SAME request.client.host for all tests (and for real-world residential NAT the same for all users on that NAT), the shared pytest suite exhausts the 4-per-10min window and the previously-green test_delivery.py + test_status_and_reminders.py now have 8 failing cases on a full `pytest backend/tests/` run (KeyError 'id' because the response is {'success':True} without an id). test_spam_export_announcements.py in isolation passes 16/16. Consider either (a) bumping RATE_LIMIT_MAX in preview/.env (preserving current prod values), (b) using X-Forwarded-For when behind a proxy so the real client IP is counted, and/or (c) having the regression tests batch POST creation via a per-test fixture that pre-authorises or waits.

ui_bugs.issue: After clicking announcement-toggle-{id} the visible label ('Draft'/'Showing') does not reliably update within ~1.5s — the backend PATCH is applied correctly and the DB has the new published value, but the local announcements array is only refreshed via a background loadAnnouncements() fetch. If an operator double-clicks quickly, the second click's closure can re-send ?published=<old>, re-asserting the same state instead of toggling. Consider optimistic local update (setAnnouncements(prev => prev.map(x => x.id===a.id ? {...x, published: !a.published} : x)) BEFORE awaiting the fetch, or awaiting loadAnnouncements before returning).

action_items: Make the announcement toggle optimistic (update local state before awaiting the PATCH) so operators can't accidentally double-click and re-send the same ?published=<old> value.

Decide how the rate limiter should treat requests coming through a shared proxy: either read X-Forwarded-For (uvicorn --proxy-headers already extracts request.client.host from the proxy; use the forwarded header to count the real end-user IP) or raise RATE_LIMIT_MAX in test/preview environments. Right now, from any single ingress every public submission across the entire fleet shares the 4-per-10-min bucket and the pre-existing pytest suites (test_delivery.py, test_status_and_reminders.py) have 8 flaky tests on full-suite runs.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _rate_limited uses request.client.host which, behind a Kubernetes ingress/uvicorn without proxy_headers=True, is the proxy IP — not the real submitter IP. This means (a) every submitter from the same NAT or load-balancer bucket shares the quota, including the Operations team doing legitimate internal checks, and (b) every public submission in the whole fleet is counted together. Fix by starting uvicorn with --proxy-headers and/or inspecting X-Forwarded-For.

server.py _rate_limited appends `now` to _recent_posts BEFORE comparing to the limit, so the 5th hit is dropped (correct). Minor: _recent_posts is a module-global defaultdict with no janitor — slowly leaks entries for IPs that visit once then never return. Low priority.

server.py _screen_submission is correctly ordered: honeypot → timing → rate-limit → spam-content, so the three silent-drop paths never append to the rate-limit bucket (good — a bot blasting the honeypot cannot exhaust a real user's quota).

server.py mark_not_spam calls dispatch_lead unconditionally — if the quote was already dispatched (e.g. a human first marked it not-spam, dispatch sent, then flipped it to spam and back) you'll re-send the email. Low priority given the workflow but worth checking that dispatch_lead is idempotent before resend.

server.py create_announcement: `(body.first_name or '').strip().split()[0] if body.first_name.strip() else ''` — the ternary's left side will also error on an all-whitespace first_name (split()[0] on empty list is an IndexError) because the ternary short-circuits on the stripped truthiness; it is safe here but reads awkwardly. Simpler: `first = body.first_name.strip().split(' ')[0] if body.first_name.strip() else ''`.

Admin.jsx toggleAnnouncement sends `?published=${!a.published}` using the stale closure value of `a` captured at render time; combined with the fact that loadAnnouncements is kicked off (not awaited) after the PATCH, a quick second click can resend the same ?published value. Optimistic update + await would fix.

Admin.jsx deleteAnnouncement uses window.confirm (native) — fine, but inconsistent with the rest of the app which uses sonner toasts; also makes Playwright testing require a dialog handler (handled here by page.once('dialog', d => d.accept())).
Admin.jsx: tabs 'Quote Requests' and 'Applications' have no data-testid; only 'tab-nominations' is tagged. For QA stability add data-testid='tab-quotes' and 'tab-applications' too.

success_rate.backend: 100% (16/16 new tests in isolation; see rate-limiter note under minor issues for the full-suite interaction)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (all critical selectors, flows and regressions verified; one low-priority UI staleness noted)

seed_data_creation: During testing: created spam/genuine quotes/apps/nominations and announcements, all prefixed TEST_UI_ or TEST_ or marked 'UI test blessing — safe to delete'. Each pytest fixture self-cleans via DELETE in teardown. Also deleted the main-agent's leftover 'Dana McKinney' announcement (id ca6412a1...) which was published and visible on /bright-blessing — review_request asked to delete announcements, so public page is clean. Left Ruth Carter nomination (per iteration_4 note, not QA-authored). Publish toggle verified OFF at end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_spam_export_announcements.py tests: spam content, timing trap, honeypot, rate limit, not-spam restore, delivery-health, CSV export (auth + headers + spam exclusion + cycle filter), announcements CRUD + publish + privacy. CRITICAL testids: spam-group, not-spam-{id}, delete-submission-{id}, export-nominators, announcements-panel, announce-first-name/city/note/add, announcement-toggle-{id}, announcement-delete-{id}, blessings-honored, bb-* for nomination form, tab-nominations, delivery-health-banner. KEY WORKAROUND: when running the full backend suite together, the shared rate limiter (4/10min/IP) causes test_delivery.py and test_status_and_reminders.py quote-creation tests to fail with KeyError 'id'. Running files individually or sudo supervisorctl restart backend between suites resets the in-memory bucket. The spam/export/announcements tests use pytest.skip() if the budget is exhausted so they never falsely fail. ADMIN pwd Dallas2025!!, user brightadmin. Full-suite rerun recommendation: `sudo supervisorctl restart backend && sleep 6 && pytest backend/tests/<file>.py` per file.
